questions.stem: When is the Business Analytics cycle from OLTP to OLAP considered complete?
options: When data reaches the Data Warehouse
When the Machine Learning model is trained
When top management sees the dashboard
Once Reverse ETL has been performed
When the campaign message is sent to customers' mobiles
questions.explanation: Most people think the cycle ends when management decides on campaigns, but it completes only once Reverse ETL is performed.

questions.stem: In the social media example, what constitutes Reverse ETL?
options: Writing back to social media in the format it accepts
Pulling all kinds of data from social media
Storing social media posts in a Data Lake
questions.explanation: Organisations pull all kinds of data from social media and never write back; writing back in the accepted format is Reverse ETL.
Business Analytics supports Decision Support Systems, with technologies running from OLTP source systems to OLAP stores.

questions.stem: In the sales campaign example of Reverse ETL, what can the customer representative see when opening the source system?
options: The Machine Learning model's accuracy score
The list of every campaign ever run
That a campaign was sent to the buyer's mobile but the buyer never reacted to it
questions.explanation: Because the campaign output was written back to the source system, the representative can see the campaign was sent and unused, and can offer another discount.

questions.stem: Where must the output of a campaign be sent for the analytics cycle to end?
questions.explanation: The cycle ends by sending the output of the campaigns back to the source systems.

questions.stem: What must Reverse ETL follow before writing back into a source system?
options: The source system's own OLTP data model
questions.explanation: Each source system has its own OLTP data model, and Reverse ETL must follow that same data model before writing back.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about Reverse ETL is NOT correct?
options: Reverse ETL is simply copying and pasting the analytics output into the source system
Reverse ETL completes the Business Analytics cycle
Reverse ETL can mean writing back to social media in the format it accepts
Reverse ETL lets source-system users see the outcome of campaigns
Reverse ETL must respect the source system's OLTP data model
questions.explanation: Reverse ETL is not just copy-pasting analytics output; each source system has its own OLTP data model that must be followed.

questions.stem: Once data has moved into stores such as a Data Lake or Data Warehouse, how are analytics performed for prediction or forecasting?
options: By reverse engineering the source schema
Using Data Science practices such as Machine Learning and Deep Learning
questions.explanation: Analytics are performed using Data Science practice, running Machine Learning, Deep Learning and other means to analyse data for prediction or forecasting.

questions.stem: What common misconception about the Business Analytics cycle does the concept of Reverse ETL correct?
options: That data must be masked before analytics
That the cycle is complete once management decides to initiate campaigns based on the analytics
That Data Lakes replace Data Warehouses
That OLTP systems cannot feed OLAP systems
questions.explanation: Most people think the cycle is complete when management decides on campaigns, but it is not complete until the results are written back through Reverse ETL.

questions.stem: Which of the following are named as OLAP-side datastores in the Business Analytics cycle?
options: Data Warehouses, Data Marts, Data Lakes, Data Lake Houses and Data Vaults
questions.explanation: The OLAP side includes Data Warehouses, Data Marts, Data Lakes, Data Lake Houses, Data Vaults, Business Vaults, Enterprise Data Hubs and Enterprise Data Fabric.
